The method relates to manufacturing a press component from an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet while preventing cracks from occurring in the inner circumferential flange of a curved portion.

In this method, the press component is produced by cold press working using a free bending method. The blank used for forming the component is made of an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet. Because such steel sheets have very high strength and limited ductility, cracks can easily occur during press forming, particularly in regions where deformation is concentrated, such as the inner circumferential flange of a curved portion.

To address this problem, a material inflow facilitating portion is formed in the blank at a position near the area that will become the inner circumferential flange of the press component. This portion is designed to promote the flow of material during the forming process. More specifically, it allows material from an end portion of the blank to flow more easily into the region that forms the inner circumferential flange.

By increasing the inflow of material into the flange area during cold press forming, the method reduces excessive tensile strain in the inner circumferential flange. As a result, the occurrence of cracks in the curved portion is suppressed, making it possible to reliably manufacture a press component from an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet using a free bending method.
outputs.L4:
A method and apparatus are provided for cold press-forming an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet into a press-formed component having a curved portion and an inner circumferential flange. The technique is particularly suitable for forming high-strength automotive structural members or similar components in which a flange must be formed along the inner side of a curved shape. In such components, the material at the inner circumferential flange is subjected to severe deformation during press forming, and cracks can easily occur because ultra-high tensile strength steel has limited ductility. The present method suppresses such cracking while maintaining the advantages of cold forming.

In the press-forming method, a blank made of an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet is placed between forming tools and is formed by free bending. The forming operation bends the blank into a predetermined curved profile while also forming a flange along an inner circumferential edge of the curved portion. During this process, the steel sheet material must flow from an end portion of the blank into the region where the inner circumferential flange is being formed. If this material flow is insufficient, excessive tensile strain is generated in the flange, particularly at or near the curved portion, resulting in cracking or tearing.

To address this problem, a material inflow facilitating portion is provided near the area of the blank that becomes the inner circumferential flange. This material inflow facilitating portion is formed or positioned so that it reduces resistance to material movement from the blank’s end portion toward the flange-forming region. As a result, during the press-forming operation, material is allowed to flow more easily into the inner circumferential flange. The increased material inflow reduces the tensile strain concentrated in the flange and improves the crack resistance of the formed component.

The material inflow facilitating portion may be provided in the blank, in the forming apparatus, or through cooperation between the blank geometry and the forming tools. For example, the blank may include a locally widened region, a relief shape, a notch, a recess, a protruding portion, or another shape that promotes material movement toward the flange-forming area. Alternatively, the press-forming apparatus may include a die, punch, pad, holder, or other tool surface configured to permit or guide controlled inflow of material during bending and flange formation. By intentionally controlling the inflow of material, the apparatus prevents excessive stretching of the inner circumferential flange.

The press-forming apparatus may include a punch for shaping the main body of the component, a die having a forming surface corresponding to the desired curved configuration, and a blank holder or pad for controlling the movement of the steel sheet during forming. The material inflow facilitating portion is arranged adjacent to the region where the inner circumferential flange is formed. During forming, the blank is bent by free bending while the material inflow facilitating portion allows the end portion of the blank to move inward or toward the flange-forming region. This controlled movement supplies additional material to the flange and alleviates localized deformation.

Because the method uses cold press forming, it avoids the cost, energy consumption, and equipment complexity associated with hot stamping or other heating-based forming processes. At the same time, it enables the forming of ultra-high tensile strength steel sheets, which are otherwise difficult to form into curved flanged components without cracking. The resulting press component has improved dimensional accuracy, high strength, and a reduced occurrence of defects in the inner circumferential flange.

This approach is especially effective for components having a curved portion where an inner flange is formed along a concave or inward-facing edge. In conventional forming, such inner circumferential flange portions are prone to cracking because the material is drawn and stretched under severe conditions. By providing the material inflow facilitating portion near the flange-forming area, the method increases the amount of material supplied from the blank’s end portion into the flange, thereby reducing strain concentration and improving formability.

Accordingly, the described method and apparatus make it possible to cold press-form ultra-high tensile strength steel sheets into complex press components with curved flanged portions while preventing or significantly reducing cracks in the inner circumferential flange. The invention improves the reliability of press forming, expands the range of shapes that can be produced from ultra-high tensile strength steel, and contributes to the manufacture of lightweight, high-strength structural parts.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a manufacturing method and apparatus for forming an ultra-high tensile strength steel press component by cold press working while preventing cracks in an inner circumferential flange of a curved portion.
counterfactuals.output: A manufacturing method and apparatus are provided for producing an ultra-high tensile strength steel press component by cold press working, the component having a curved portion and an inner circumferential flange formed along an inner peripheral edge of the curved portion. The method includes placing a steel sheet blank between a die and a punch, restraining a predetermined region of the blank with a blank holder, and press-forming the blank while controlling material flow toward the inner circumferential flange. During forming, a compressive or reduced-tensile stress state is imparted to a flange-forming region at the inner side of the curved portion by a flange forming surface, a draw-in control surface, and/or a locally movable forming member, thereby suppressing circumferential tensile strain concentration that would otherwise cause cracking. The apparatus includes a punch, a die having a curved forming portion, a blank holder configured to regulate sheet inflow, and a flange forming portion shaped or driven to form the inner circumferential flange while distributing strain in the flange-forming region. Accordingly, even a steel sheet having ultra-high tensile strength can be cold-formed into a press component including a curved inner flange with improved crack resistance and dimensional accuracy.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical summary of an invention involving free bending press working of a steel sheet blank, where material inflow is facilitated near a flange on the inner side of a curved press component.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention concerns a press-forming method for producing a curved steel sheet component having a flange along the inner side of the curve.

A steel sheet blank is subjected to free bending press working, in which the blank is bent into a curved shape while portions of the material are allowed to move rather than being fully clamped. In particular, material inflow is promoted in a region adjacent to the flange on the inner circumferential side of the curved component. By permitting this controlled inflow during forming, excessive tensile strain and thinning near the inner flange are reduced, while compressive deformation that could cause wrinkling is better managed.

The technique improves formability of high-strength steel sheets and enables accurate production of curved press parts with inner-side flanges, such as automotive structural members, while suppressing cracking, wrinkling, and dimensional defects.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent claim-like description for a method of manufacturing a press component from an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet that avoids flange cracking during cold press forming.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **A method of manufacturing a press component from an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet**, the method comprising:

   preparing a steel sheet blank having a tensile strength of not less than 980 MPa;

   defining, in the steel sheet blank, a flange-forming region including an edge portion that is to be subjected to tensile deformation during cold press forming;

   locally modifying the flange-forming region before cold press forming so as to increase stretch-flange formability of the edge portion relative to an unmodified portion of the steel sheet blank;

   thereafter cold press forming the steel sheet blank in a press die to form a press component including a bent or drawn main body portion and a flange portion extending from the main body portion; and

   forming the flange portion while suppressing crack initiation at the edge portion of the flange-forming region.

2. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the local modifying comprises locally heating the flange-forming region to a temperature lower than an austenite transformation temperature of the steel sheet, thereby tempering or softening the flange-forming region without substantially reducing strength of the main body portion.

3. **The method according to claim 2**, wherein the flange-forming region is locally heated by laser irradiation, induction heating, resistance heating, infrared heating, or contact heating.

4. **The method according to claim 2**, wherein the flange-forming region is heated to a temperature of 300°C to 750°C and subsequently cooled before the cold press forming.

5. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the local modifying comprises removing or reducing a work-hardened layer or damaged layer formed on the edge portion during blanking or shearing.

6. **The method according to claim 5**, wherein the removing or reducing comprises shaving, grinding, machining, laser trimming, fine blanking, or polishing the edge portion before the cold press forming.

7. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the steel sheet blank is formed by punching or cutting a precursor sheet, and a cutting clearance, cutting direction, or cut-edge orientation is selected such that a fracture surface of the edge portion is positioned away from a region of maximum tensile strain during formation of the flange portion.

8. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the cold press forming comprises drawing, bending, stretch flanging, burring, hemming, or a combination thereof, performed at room temperature without heating the entire steel sheet blank.

9. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the flange-forming region has, after the local modifying and before the cold press forming, a hardness lower than a hardness of the main body portion.

10. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet comprises a martensitic steel sheet, a dual-phase steel sheet, a transformation-induced plasticity steel sheet, a complex-phase steel sheet, or a hot-stamped steel sheet.

11. **The method according to claim 1**, further comprising trimming the press component after the cold press forming to form a final edge of the flange portion.

12. **The method according to claim 1**, wherein the local modifying is performed only in a portion of the steel sheet blank corresponding to the flange portion, such that a remaining portion of the press component maintains ultra-high tensile strength after forming.

13. **A method of manufacturing an automotive structural press component**, comprising:

   blanking an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet to form a blank having an edge region to be stretch-flanged;

   locally softening the edge region by applying heat to the edge region while leaving a central load-bearing region of the blank substantially unsoftened;

   placing the blank in a cold press forming die; and

   cold forming the blank to produce an automotive structural component having a flange, wherein the locally softened edge region accommodates tensile deformation during formation of the flange and thereby prevents flange cracking.

14. **The method according to claim 13**, wherein the automotive structural component is a pillar reinforcement, rocker reinforcement, bumper reinforcement, roof rail component, side member, cross member, or suspension-related press component.

15. **A press component manufactured by the method according to claim 1**, wherein the press component includes a flange portion formed from a locally modified flange-forming region of an ultra-high tensile strength steel sheet, the flange portion being free of visible edge cracks after cold press forming.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an apparatus and method for press-forming a curved automotive steel component, including a material inflow facilitating portion that helps form an inner circumferential flange without cracks.
counterfactuals.output:
An apparatus for press-forming a curved automotive steel component may include a press die set configured to form a steel blank into a curved member having an inner circumferential flange, for example a curved frame, reinforcement, pillar-related part, or wheel-arch-type structural component.

The apparatus includes:

1. **A punch**
   - Having a forming surface corresponding to the inside shape of the curved component.
   - The punch includes a curved main forming portion and a flange-forming portion along the inner circumferential side of the component.

2. **A die**
   - Arranged opposite the punch.
   - Having a die cavity or forming surface corresponding to the outside shape of the curved component.
   - The die cooperates with the punch to bend, draw, or stretch-form the blank into the desired curved profile.

3. **A blank holder or pressure pad**
   - Holds a peripheral portion of the steel blank during forming.
   - Controls material flow from the blank edge into the forming region.
   - The holding force may be locally reduced or shaped so that material can flow preferentially toward the inner circumferential flange region.

4. **An inner circumferential flange-forming section**
   - Forms an upstanding, depending, or laterally bent flange along the inner radius of the curved component.
   - This region is prone to cracking because the inner circumferential edge is subjected to severe tensile strain or stretch-flange deformation during press forming.

5. **A material inflow facilitating portion**
   - Provided near the region where the inner circumferential flange is formed.
   - This portion is shaped or arranged so that additional blank material can flow into the inner circumferential flange-forming region during pressing.
   - It may be formed as a locally recessed portion, relief portion, bead-free portion, low-restriction holding area, widened clearance portion, pocket portion, or locally curved slack-forming portion in the die, punch, or blank holder.
   - Its function is to reduce excessive stretching at the inner circumferential flange by supplying material from an adjacent area of the blank.

In operation, the material inflow facilitating portion prevents the inner circumferential flange from being formed only by stretching the blank edge. Instead, material is allowed to move into the flange-forming region, reducing tensile strain concentration and suppressing edge cracking.

A representative method includes the following steps:

1. **Preparing a steel blank**
   - A flat steel sheet blank, such as a high-strength automotive steel sheet, is cut to a predetermined outline.
   - The blank may include an edge portion that will become the inner circumferential flange of the curved component.

2. **Placing the blank in the die set**
   - The blank is positioned between the punch and die.
   - A portion of the blank is held by the blank holder or pressure pad.

3. **Controlling material flow**
   - During the initial stage of pressing, the blank holder restrains general movement of the blank.
   - At the material inflow facilitating portion, however, the resistance to material movement is reduced or a slack-forming space is provided.
   - As a result, material near the inner circumferential side is permitted to flow toward the flange-forming region.

4. **Forming the curved main body**
   - The punch and die move relative to each other to form the blank into a curved shape.
   - The main wall, web, or channel portion of the automotive component is shaped while material flow is controlled.

5. **Forming the inner circumferential flange**
   - The inner circumferential edge portion is bent or drawn into a flange by the flange-forming section.
   - Because material has been supplied from the material inflow facilitating portion, the flange is formed with reduced tensile strain.
   - The risk of cracking at the edge of the inner circumferential flange is thereby lowered.

6. **Completing the press stroke and removing the part**
   - After the flange and curved body are fully formed, the press opens.
   - The formed automotive steel component is removed.
   - If necessary, trimming, piercing, or calibration may be performed afterward.

In this apparatus and method, the key feature is that the inner circumferential flange is not forced to elongate excessively during forming. The material inflow facilitating portion intentionally permits or promotes local inflow of steel sheet material into the flange-forming area, thereby improving formability and enabling crack-free formation of a curved high-strength steel automotive component.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an AI-generated patent abstract about cold press working a blank by a free bending method to manufacture a press component with improved material flow into an inner flange of a curved portion.
counterfactuals.output: A method of manufacturing a press component includes cold press working a metal blank by a free bending process in which at least a curved portion of the blank is bent without being fully restrained between opposed forming surfaces. The blank is formed into a component having an outer flange, an inner flange, and a curved wall portion extending along a longitudinal direction. During bending, a forming tool applies a bending load while permitting controlled displacement of material toward an inner circumferential side of the curved portion. A material-flow promoting region, including at least one of a locally reduced restraining force, a clearance, a draw-in allowance, or a preformed surplus-material portion, is provided adjacent to the inner flange so that material is supplied into the inner flange as the curved portion is formed. This suppresses thinning, cracking, wrinkling, and dimensional deviation at the inner flange, thereby enabling stable manufacture of a high-strength press component having improved shape accuracy and flange formability.
